articles.summary: Alcon Acquires Neurotech and ENCELTO, the Only FDA-Approved Treatment for MacTel Type 2 Anonymous (not verified) Tue, 10/20/2026 - 20:36 Tuesday, October 20, 2026 Expands Alcon’s retina portfolio with ENCELTO, an encapsulated cell therapy intended for surgical implantation in the eye for patients with MacTel Type 2, a rare retinal disease Alcon's established presence and expertise in surgical retina is expected to accelerate commercialization and patient access Broadens Alcon’s offering in retinal disease GENEVA--(BUSINESS WIRE)-- Alcon (SIX/NYSE: ALC), the global leader in eye care dedicated to helping people see brilliantly, today announced it has acquired Neurotech Pharmaceuticals, Inc., a company focused on developing innovative cell therapies for chronic and neurodegenerative eye diseases. This acquisition expands Alcon's retina portfolio with ENCELTO™ (revakinagene taroretcel-lwey), the first and only U.S. FDA-approved treatment for adults with idiopathic Macular Telangiectasia Type 2 (MacTel), a rare, progressive retinal disease that leads to irreversible central vision loss that has historically had no approved treatment options. ENCELTO is an encapsulated cell therapy that is intended for surgical intravitreal implantation. The FDA granted ENCELTO priority review status and Orphan Drug designation and approved ENCELTO under a Biologics License Application (BLA) in March 2025. It currently is available in the U.S. only. "Neurotech's innovative platform sits at the intersection of cell therapy, pharmaceuticals, and surgery, making it a highly complementary addition to our current capabilities and advancing our vision for the future of retinal disease treatment,” said David Endicott, Chief Executive Officer of Alcon. "By combining Neurotech’s groundbreaking science and established commercial footprint with Alcon's global reach and clinical expertise, we can help bring this innovation to more patients whose vision is threatened by MacTel." It is estimated that there are approximately 25,000 diagnosed MacTel patients in the U.S. with 2,000-3,000 patients newly diagnosed annually.1-3,† Until ENCELTO, there have been no FDA-approved treatments for MacTel patients. ENCELTO continuously releases a protein called recombinant human ciliary neurotrophic factor (rhCNTF) that can directly reach the retina, the light-sensitive part of the eye. CNTF helps protect certain cells in the retina, supporting their health and reducing the loss of light-sensing cells known as photoreceptors. “ENCELTO addresses a significant unmet need for MacTel patients,” said Dan Miller, MD, PhD, Distinguished Fellow, Research & Development, Alcon. “Alcon's presence in surgical retina combined with its dedication to innovation make them the ideal partner to broaden access to this important therapy.” “This milestone significantly advances Neurotech’s mission to bring ENCELTO to patients suffering from this debilitating disease,“ said Richard Small, Chief Executive Officer of Neurotech Pharmaceuticals, Inc. “Alcon’s global scale, commercial capabilities and scientific expertise will expand and facilitate patient access to ENCELTO, and I’m grateful to the entire Neurotech team, as well as the physicians, investigators, patients, and advocates within the MacTel community whose dedication has made this achievement possible.” As part of the acquisition, Alcon paid $550 million to acquire Neurotech Pharmaceuticals, Inc. Alcon may be required to make additional contingent payments, including upon the achievement of commercial milestones. Alcon expects the transaction to be modestly accretive to net sales growth and slightly dilutive to core diluted eps in 2027, and accretive thereafter. Goldman Sachs & Co, served as financial advisor to Alcon and Gibson, Dunn & Crutcher LLP served as legal advisor to Alcon. J.P. Morgan Securities, LLC. served as lead financial advisor to Neurotech, and Cravath Swaine & Moore LLP served as lead legal advisor to Neurotech. Other advisors to Neurotech included Rothschild & Co, Ropes & Gray LLP, Fenwick & West LLP and Elrifi Law PLLC. About Alcon Alcon helps people see brilliantly. As the global leader in eye care with a heritage spanning over 75 years, we offer the broadest portfolio of products to enhance sight and improve people’s lives. Our Surgical and Vision Care products touch the lives of more than 260 million people in over 140 countries and territories each year living with conditions like cataracts, glaucoma, retinal diseases and refractive errors. Our more than 25,000 associates are enhancing the quality of life through innovative products, partnerships with Eye Care Professionals and programs that advance access to quality eye care. Learn more at www.alcon.com . About Neurotech Pharmaceuticals, Inc. Neurotech Pharmaceuticals, Inc. is a private biotech company focused on developing transformative therapies for chronic eye diseases. The core platform technology, Encapsulated Cell Therapy (ECT) is a first in class, drug delivery platform designed to slow the progression of MacTel and other chronic eye diseases. Learn more at https://www.neurotechpharmaceuticals.com . About Macular Telangiectasia Type 2 (MacTel) Macular Telangiectasia Type 2 (MacTel), or idiopathic macular telangiectasia type 2, is a bilateral, neurodegenerative disease in adults with characteristic localized retinal degeneration, a group of diseases that cause the gradual loss of cells in the retina, resulting in vision loss and secondary alterations of the retinal vasculature, the network of blood vessels that supplies oxygen and nutrients to the retina.4 About Encapsulated Cell Therapy (ECT) Neurotech’s ECT platform is a cell-based gene therapy delivery system designed to provide long-term, sustained delivery of therapeutic proteins for the treatment of chronic eye diseases. This versatile platform consists of a small, semi-permeable capsule containing proprietary allogeneic retinal pigment epithelium (RPE) cells genetically engineered to produce specific therapeutic proteins for targeted disease treatment. Indications and Usage ENCELTO is an allogeneic encapsulated cell-based gene therapy indicated for the treatment of adults with idiopathic macular telangiectasia type 2 (MacTel). IMPORTANT SAFETY INFORMATION ENCELTO is inserted into the eye as an outpatient surgical procedure performed by an eye surgeon experienced in vitreoretinal surgery. If removal of ENCELTO is necessary, the removal surgery must also be done by an eye surgeon experienced in vitreoretinal surgery in an operating room as an outpatient surgery. Please be advised that ENCELTO and the surgical insertion has related risks such as, but not limited to, endophthalmitis (eye infection), retinal tear and detachment (retina tears and potentially separates from the eye wall resulting in vision loss) vitreous hemorrhage, implant, extrusion, suture-related issues, temporary or permanent loss of vision, accelerated cataract formation and delayed dark adaptation Patients may report side effects to the Food and Drug Administration (FDA) at 1-800-FDA-1088. articles.summary: FDA Approves Alcon’s BRYTLY Redness Reliever Eye Drops for Up to 12 Hours of Whiter, Brighter-Looking Eyes Anonymous (not verified) Fri, 10/16/2026 - 19:58 Friday, October 16, 2026 One drop works to significantly reduce redness, with results lasting up to 12 hours1 Lasts up to 50% longer than Lumify1-2,* Expands Alcon's portfolio of consumer eye care solutions and will be available in major retailers nationwide and online in the coming months GENEVA--(BUSINESS WIRE)-- Alcon (SIX/NYSE: ALC), the global leader in eye care dedicated to helping people see brilliantly, today announced that the U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA) has approved BRYTLY® Redness Reliever Eye Drops. With one drop, BRYTLY works in just one minute to significantly reduce redness and delivers up to 12 hours of whiter, brighter-looking eyes.1 Additionally, BRYTLY lasts up to 50% longer than Lumify.1-2,* The approval brings a differentiated new option to the over the counter (OTC) redness-relief category and expands Alcon’s portfolio of trusted consumer eye care products. FDA Approves Alcon’s BRYTLY Redness Reliever Eye Drops Beauty and wellness routines are increasingly converging, with consumers looking for products that combine visible results, clinical validation and everyday convenience. Research has also found that visible eye redness can influence perceptions of healthiness and attractiveness, creating new relevance for the eyes as part of an overall appearance and wellness routine.3 BRYTLY brings a clinically proven option to this evolving space, by reducing redness and helping eyes look whiter and brighter with results that can last throughout the day, up to 12 hours. “Consumers invest in products that help them look and feel their best, and the appearance of their eyes can be an important part of that,” said Jonathan Balch, General Manager, Ocular Health & Pharmaceuticals, Alcon. “This FDA approval marks an exciting milestone for Alcon. With BRYTLY, we’re bringing Alcon’s trusted eye care expertise to consumers who want to reduce eye redness and want their eyes to look whiter and brighter. BRYTLY is designed to deliver simple, long-lasting redness reduction that can help consumers feel confident in how their eyes look throughout the day.” BRYTLY contains no bleaches or dyes and is clinically proven to be safe and effective when used as directed.1 Studies also demonstrated a low risk of redness rebound and tachyphylaxis when used as directed.4-5 “When patients ask about eye whiteners, they want a product they can trust to work effectively and fit into their day,” said Selina McGee**, founder and chief optometrist of Bespoke Vision in Edmond, Oklahoma. “BRYTLY gives Eye Care Professionals a clinically proven option to recommend, with demonstrated safety and efficacy and long-lasting redness reduction from a single drop.” BRYTLY is expected to be available at major retailers nationwide and online in the coming months, and in additional markets in the future. articles.summary: SYSTANE PRO Preservative-Free Demonstrates Clinically Comparable Dry Eye Symptom Relief to MIEBO (perfluorohexyloctane ophthalmic solution) in a Prospective, Randomized Clinical Study sandra.hoffer Thu, 10/01/2026 - 15:27 Friday, October 2, 2026 SYSTANE PRO Preservative-Free (PF) demonstrated non-inferiority to MIEBO^ (perfluorohexyloctane ophthalmic solution) in relieving dry eye symptoms at two weeks and one month1,* Findings provide Eye Care Professionals with comparative clinical evidence supporting SYSTANE PRO PF for patients with dry eye1 FORT WORTH, October 2, 2026 — Alcon (SIX/NYSE: ALC), the global leader in eye care dedicated to helping people see brilliantly, today announced new investigator-initiated clinical data demonstrating that SYSTANE® PRO Preservative-Free (PF), an Alcon brand, provided clinically comparable dry eye symptom relief to MIEBO^ (perfluorohexyloctane ophthalmic solution), meeting the study's primary endpoint of non-inferiority at both two weeks and one month based on Ocular Surface Disease Index (OSDI) scores.1,* The findings were presented at the American Academy of Optometry 2026 Annual Meeting (AAO; Anaheim; September 30-October 3). “These results provide Eye Care Professionals (ECPs) with meaningful comparative evidence when considering treatment options for patients with dry eye disease,” said Anna Tichenor,*** OD, PhD, FAAO, Assistant Professor and Chief of the IUSO Dry Eye Clinic, and lead investigator of the study. “Based on these findings, I can confidently recommend SYSTANE PRO PF as a first-line treatment option for patients in my practice with dry eye symptoms, particularly given the clinically comparable dry eye symptom relief to prescription perfluorohexyloctane demonstrated in this study. For ECPs with patients facing cost or insurance-related access barriers, Systane Pro PF may offer an accessible approach to dry eye symptom relief.” Dry eye disease (DED) is one of the most common ocular surface disorders, affecting an estimated 39 million people in the United States and 1.6 billion globally.2,3 Common symptoms can include dryness, irritation, burning and fluctuating vision, which can interfere with everyday activities such as reading, night driving, using digital devices, working and socializing.4-6 DED can also affect contact lens wear and may impact a patient’s ability to undergo cataract or refractive surgery.4-6 Yet only 13% of patients with DED feel their condition is well-managed, underscoring the need for effective treatment options that can help address the diverse needs of people living with dry eye disease.7,† This head-to-head study*** was a prospective, randomized, double-masked, multicenter clinical study that evaluated 256 dry eye patients with moderate-to-severe symptoms.1 Patients were randomized to SYSTANE PRO PF or perfluorohexyloctane four times daily in both eyes and were assessed at baseline, two weeks and one month.1 The primary endpoint evaluated non-inferiority of SYSTANE PRO PF versus perfluorohexyloctane on OSDI symptom scores, using a prespecified non-inferiority margin of 7.3 units.1 SYSTANE PRO PF demonstrated clinically meaningful dry eye symptom relief while proving to be non-inferior to perfluorohexyloctane.1,* Both treatment groups achieved statistically significant and clinically meaningful reductions in OSDI symptoms (p≤0.001) at two weeks and sustained through one month.1,* SYSTANE PRO PF is available over the counter (OTC) in the U.S., Canada and other markets. MIEBO^ is available by prescription in the U.S., while perfluorohexyloctane is offered OTC in certain markets outside of the U.S. “These findings underscore the strength of SYSTANE PRO PF, backed by a rigorous, independently conducted randomized clinical study.” said Sarika Sood, Vice President of Global Medical Affairs and Health Economics and Outcomes Research at Alcon. “The results add to the growing body of evidence supporting SYSTANE PRO PF and reinforce the strength of Alcon’s comprehensive dry eye portfolio.” SYSTANE PRO PF is formulated to provide sustained hydration, restore tear film stability†† and protect against further irritation of dry eyes.8,9 To learn more about Alcon’s dry eye offerings, visit systane.myalcon.com . articles.summary: Alcon Children’s Vision Center and Lighthouse for the Blind: Expanding Opportunity Through Eye Care sandra.hoffer Tue, 10/20/2026 - 16:07 Story Headline Alcon Children’s Vision Center and Lighthouse for the Blind: Expanding Opportunity Through Eye Care Story Teaser Summary Since 2021, Alcon Children's Vision Center (ACVC) and Lighthouse for the Blind in Fort Worth have partnered to help students access the eye care they need while creating meaningful employment opportunities for individuals who are blind or visually impaired. Story Date Thu, 10/22/2026 - 12:00 Featured 1 Category Vision for the World Hero image Since 2021, Alcon Children’s Vision Center (ACVC) and Lighthouse for the Blind in Fort Worth, Texas, have partnered to support community eye care and create meaningful employment opportunities for individuals who are blind or visually impaired. ACVC was formed through a partnership between Alcon and the Fort Worth Independent School District (FWISD) to overcome barriers in accessing eye care for students in need. Through the partnership, students receive vision screening by Alcon Associates, follow-up care coordinated by ACVC and prescription glasses from Lighthouse for the Blind at no cost to them, their families or the school district. Through a shared purpose of expanding access to eye care, the relationship has blossomed into a multifaceted partnership connecting Alcon’s commitment to help people See Brilliantly with Lighthouse for the Blind’s mission to help people with significant vision loss live with more independence. Today, this partnership comes to life with every pair of glasses a student receives. Since the start of the children’s mission program, ACVC has provided support for approximately 115,000 students through vision screenings, demonstrating the reach of its efforts to expand access to eye care. More Than a Pair of Glasses Lighthouse for the Blind has had a long-standing history of creating opportunities for people with vision loss. That commitment remains at the heart of Lighthouse’s work today. In 2017, Lighthouse launched the Lighthouse Lab to create nontraditional jobs for people who are blind while providing employees with transferable, technical skills. Two years later, Mission Optical , a social enterprise within the Lighthouse Lab, was created to manufacture prescription eyewear while creating meaningful employment for people who are visually impaired. It also expands access to glasses for community members experiencing financial hardship. Creating an Eye Care Partnership Through Mission Optical, Lighthouse optical staff work directly with ACVC’s program team to process and fulfill custom prescription orders. The Lighthouse Lab serves as the exclusive laboratory vendor supporting prescription eyewear for students identified through the ACVC eye exams. For the children receiving those glasses, the impact can extend well beyond clearer eyesight. “Unlike other school-based vision or charitable programs, ACVC's core mission is to be more than a quick fix for students with a vision need; rather, it serves as a bridge between students, families, schools, and the eye care system.” – Kendall D. Stout O.D., lead optometrist at Alcon Children’s Vision Center At Lighthouse, fulfilling those prescriptions creates another form of opportunity. Lab employees manufacture custom eyewear while developing specialized skills and earning competitive wages and benefits. The lab can produce a wide range of prescription lenses such as single-vision, bifocal, progressive and low-vision glasses. Each order represents an impact on both sides of the process. “Alcon’s involvement is a true full-circle partnership. By designating the Lighthouse Lab as their exclusive lab vendor for FWISD vision screenings through Mission Optical, Alcon directly connects its outreach with local job creation and community service, ensuring every pair of glasses funded for a student also sustains a job for a visually impaired adult in Fort Worth.” – Brian Talkington*, lab manager at Lighthouse Optical Finishing Lab Helping Kids See Brilliantly For ACVC, the result is a partnership that represents what the organization has worked for, ensuring that treatments for visual impairments are available for those who may otherwise struggle to afford it. For some families, that can be surprising. One ACVC team member recalled a parent asking how much she owed after her child’s appointment and being visibly relieved to learn there was no charge. One child who came to the program was about 2 years old and had severe refractive error in both eyes. She was frightened during the fitting process, and when her glasses were placed on her face, she initially cried. Then, as she began to realize she could see the people and objects around her clearly, she stopped. "She was in awe of everything around her,” Courtney Dziurawiec, the optician at ACVC recalled. “Everyone was so excited to see what a transformation this would be for this little girl’s life.” Stories like this illustrate why the partnership reaches beyond clear vision. Access to appropriate eye care can affect a person’s whole life, including academic performance and confidence in a child’s ability to engage fully in the classroom. “ACVC’s mission is Helping kids learn by helping kids see Brilliantly. Lighthouse for the Blind helps with that through making the glasses in a timely and accurate fashion. The staff at Lighthouse for the Blind has been extremely helpful.” – Courtney Dziurawiec, optician at Alcon Children’s Vision Center Alcon and Lighthouse have a shared goal to continue expanding their impact by reaching more communities and helping ensure that access to eye care can open doors for students and their families. The next chapter will center around increasing access to screenings, comprehensive eye exams and eyewear in Fort Worth, Texas and beyond. About Lighthouse for the Blind Serving the 78,000 blind or significantly visually impaired people living in Tarrant and surrounding Texas counties, the organization provides education, adaptive technology training, independent living skills, rehabilitation services, and employment for children, adults and elderly. Employment has been central to that mission since its founding, creating opportunities for people with significant visual impairments while supporting the broader community. About Alcon Children’s Vision Center Alcon Children’s Vision Center is a partnership between the Alcon Foundation and Fort Worth ISD that provides comprehensive eye exams and eyewear at no cost to FWISD students unable to obtain care through insurance or local providers. The center provides services at elementary schools across the district and through its Fort Worth clinic, helping students access the vision care they need. *Paid Alcon consultant Related Story Alcon and Aravind: Expanding Access Through Education Building More Than Homes: How Alcon and Habitat for Humanity Are Strengthening Communities Through Alcon in Action Search Description Since 2021, Alcon Children's Vision Center (ACVC) and Lighthouse for the Blind in Fort Worth have partnered to help students access the eye care they need while creating meaningful employment opportunities for individuals who are blind or visually impaired.
